export_evidence: importkey.com/countries/india/shah-enterprise shows "Total Shipments 481 Records detected" with rows such as "2026-02-26 SHAH ENTERPRISE APEX GLOBAL SOLUTIONS SIEMENS 6ES5316-8MA12- AHEMDABAD AIR ACC INAMD4, India SHARJAH, UNITED ARAB EMIRATES 85381010 1060175" — but the same page lists mutually unrelated counterparties (Yantai Fenglin, Tronox Bunbury, Pegasus Ltd, Amazon.com FBA warehouses, Jamyang Agro Food Bhutan, Abdul Rahman Dwitama Global Persada Singapore) and a Kolkata address "58 A,PADDAPUKUR ROAD", i.e. it is an aggregated name-match page, not one legal entity. No row carries HS 847990 and none can be tied to a Gujarat company. Slug variants /shah-enterprise-gujarat, /shah-enterprise-ahmedabad and /shah-enterprise-2 returned empty record tables ("Loading..." / no rows). Source counter: 481 shipments claimed on the aggregate page; rows actually readable and attributable to the Gujarat entity: 0.
domestic_evidence: No GST turnover band, GeM/CPPP tender award, contract or annual-report split could be retrieved for a Gujarat entity named SHAH ENTERPRISE. Search tooling was unavailable (DuckDuckGo/searx returned "Connection refused" on both queries) and volza.com and eximpedia.app returned HTTP 403, so no domestic supply record was seen.
note: Name is highly ambiguous: at least four distinct businesses trade as 'Shah Enterprise' (Kolkata chemical importer, Gujarat entity, Bhutan-linked agro buyer, Singapore-linked shipper). The declared HS 847990 (parts of machinery for working rubber/plastics or mineral products) is not corroborated by any record seen — the only visible HS codes are 85381010, 32061110, 39123912, 39079120, all on the Kolkata-linked aggregate page. Per Rule 5, no shipment is treated as confirmed: export_status and domestic_status are 'unknown' rather than 'confirmed' or 'none_found', because the entity cannot be isolated in public data — this is a data-attribution gap, not evidence of absence. No CIN, PAN, GSTIN, revenue or export volume is public in the sources read; all left null, nothing invented. Recommended next step: obtain the supplier's GSTIN/IEC and re-query customs data by IEC, which would resolve the name collision.
